content.title: About
content.content: Vegetarian stew is a hearty dish made from a variety of vegetables, legumes, and spices. It is rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making it suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking to reduce meat consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional stews are cooked slowly to allow vegetables to fully develop their flavors.
Legumes such as lentils or beans add protein and make the dish more filling.
A mix of carrots, celery, tomatoes, and zucchini provides a wide range of vitamins and antioxidants.
Vegetarian stew can be repurposed as a base for cold soups or casseroles.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

items.title: Plant‑based protein source
items.content: Legumes supply a complete set of amino acids essential for muscle and tissue health.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Vegetables and legumes provide B6, folate, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, carrots, and spices like turmeric are rich in antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of meat makes the stew suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, peas, or lentils.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Certain vegetables (e.g., spinach) can increase oxalate levels, which may be a concern for kidney‑stone‑prone people.

items.title: Potential sodium levels
items.content: Using prepared broths or soy sauce can raise the salt content of the stew.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot as a main dish or alongside whole‑grain cereals, quinoa, rice, or bread. It stores well in the fridge for reheating and can also be used as a filling for pies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the stew in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before consuming.
